clue.text: A living thing about to have almost what any type of actor is doing. (One hopes the kids are!)

definitions.text: what any type of actor is doing
definitions.note: an actor in the broad sense is anyone who acts, and acting is behaving

indicators.note: the word for a living thing goes around the shortened word

parts.note: a living thing is a being

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A wry aside about children and actors, with the hope that the kids are being good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' leaves HAV, which 'about' tells you to wrap the living thing around. 'Actor' means anyone who acts; the parenthesis is a playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is simply to act or conduct oneself, which is what any agent who acts is doing.

clue.text: Another name for a bollard, to possibly rely on the result in an untasteful way.

parts.note: a bitt is a post on a ship's deck for fastening ropes, a kind of bollard

indicators.note: possibly shows the word could be spelt in another order

parts.note: the word taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Leaning on a bollard and finding the outcome in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness is a sharp, unpleasant taste, so doing something bitterly is done in a way that tastes bad.

clue.text: The girl objectively gets on as a real bird!

parts.note: her is the object form of she, the girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl getting along like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' is grammar: the object pronoun, not 'she'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading species of water fowl, an actual feathered creature rather than slang for a girl.

clue.text: A musician might play one with 10, possibly (only the last half) in a pretty wild way!

parts.note: a viol is an old stringed instrument

indicators.note: possibly signals the number's letters arranged differently

parts.note: the number ten written as a word

indicators.note: only the last half of the word is kept, its first half dropped

parts.note: the word taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician playing wildly alongside ten others, or half of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 is the number, not a cross-reference: 'possibly' turns TEN into ENT. 'The last half' of ONLY is LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something violently is doing it with great force and wildness.

clue.text: Worthy of your attention, but can't do much about anything.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into NOT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable deserves to be noticed, which is what worthy of attention means.

clue.text: Taw, possibly–proving Mable is about right!

indicators.note: the name is wrapped about the letter for right

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Mable proving herself correct about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is about' puts MABLE around R. A taw is a large shooting marble in the children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A taw is one particular kind of playing ball used in the game of marbles, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Go carefully over the figures, in Paris to get said properly.

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: Checking accounts in Paris and getting the pronunciation right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' covers both pieces: both are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a careful official inspection of financial accounts, here used as a verb.

clue.text: A real looney from Rio? (Three-sided, too!)

definitions.text: A real looney from Rio? (Three-sided, too!)

parts.words: A real looney from Rio? (Three-sided, too
parts.note: a 'nut' is slang for a crazy person; this one comes from the country whose city is Rio, and the actual nut has a three-sided shell

explanation.walkthrough: Rio de Janeiro is in Brazil, and nut is slang for a looney; the real nut of that name has a three-sided shell.
explanation.definitionFit: This large edible seed from a South American tree has a hard, roughly triangular shell.

clue.text: Dash to sing badly for a type of banner.

parts.note: an en is a printer's dash, the en dash

indicators.note: badly shows the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the word taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Rushing off to sing out of tune under a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show nationality.

clue.text: A large number of what might get charged in Java commonly.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a fee is a sum charged

explanation.surface: A large sum charged to someone on the island of Java.
explanation.walkthrough: Java is common American slang for coffee, not the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is a colloquial word for the drink brewed from roasted beans, from the island that once grew it.

clue.text: The players might hope for a good one, as things develop.

definitions.text: The players might hope for a good one
definitions.meaning: first meaning: performers hope a good number of people come to watch
second meaning; the clue treats the noun as that verb phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into the phrasal verb: as things turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the attendance at an event, which any cast or team hopes will be large.

clue.text: Trials, otherwise throws out the cards.

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll be late'
a dealer deals, handing out the cards

explanation.surface: A card player's trials, or else the dealing of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordeals are painful experiences that test someone, the same sense as trials.

clue.text: Pyle, for instance, being one point in the lake.

indicators.note: the compass letter is placed in the lake's name

parts.note: Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes
N for north, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone named Pyle standing at a point in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts N inside ERIE. Ernie Pyle was the American war correspondent of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is the first name of the war reporter Pyle, so the definition works by example of a person with that name.

clue.text: Madame hopes the new dress will, which is proper.

definitions.text: Madame hopes the new dress will
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The first half completes itself with the answer split in two: the dress will be fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something befitting is suitable for the occasion, which is what proper means here.

clue.text: The series of items has the last letter intended for the composer.

indicators.note: the series holds the letter within it

parts.note: a list is a series of items
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A list whose final entry is a letter set aside for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' puts Z inside LIST. Franz Liszt was the Hungarian pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Liszt was a celebrated nineteenth-century Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: The ego takes over when one so acts, and is fleshly, perhaps.

definitions.text: The ego takes over when one so acts
definitions.note: an adverb, standing for 'so' in 'acts so'

indicators.note: perhaps indicates the letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark on the ego taking over when someone behaves in a carnal way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with no regard for others but only for oneself is putting the ego first.

clue.text: What's the point to darning your socks, for example–at least changing things for the better!

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
darning socks is an example of mending clothes

explanation.surface: A sigh about the pointlessness of darning socks, which at least improves them.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve, usually a text, so emending is changing for the better.

clue.text: Zen: do it! It straightened out an operatic composer.

indicators.note: sorting out a muddle rearranges these letters

parts.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: A Zen command to just do it, which put a composer right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straightened out' rearranges ZEN DO IT IT. Gaetano Donizetti was the Italian composer of Lucia di Lammermoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Donizetti was an Italian bel canto composer who wrote dozens of operas.

clue.text: Bone up on being given a name–being given a name.

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part sits on top of the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy
called means named

explanation.surface: Swotting up on how things get their names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone up' looks like the idiom for study, but it is the Latin bone read 'up' to give SO, placed 'on' the second piece in this down entry. The setter deliberately repeats the phrase as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: So-called describes something given a particular name, often doubtfully.

clue.text: As for the kids they like such–which might be the hour for Hamlet.

definitions.text: As for the kids they like such

indicators.note: the hour comes before what it is set aside for, so the play is set in front

parts.note: Hamlet is a play by Shakespeare
an hour is a time

explanation.surface: Children enjoying a period of the day, which might also be when Hamlet is staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Children love the break in the day set aside for games, the recess period at school.

clue.text: Here in Paris, the east of Paris is most frigid…

parts.note: ici is French for here
est is French for east

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Paris, the east side is the coldest.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciest is the superlative of icy, meaning the coldest, the same as most frigid.

clue.text: …so such fancy garments might be welcome!

definitions.text: …so such fancy garments might be welcome!

parts.words: so such fancy garments might be welcome
parts.note: following the clue before about the coldest place, luxurious white fur wraps would be welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the previous one: where it is coldest, fur would be welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat, used for luxurious robes and wraps.

clue.text: It could be the preface to a big blow-up, or a least the intro for such.

definitions.text: It could be the preface to a big blow-up, or a least the intro for such.

parts.words: It could be the preface to a big blow-up, or a least the intro for such
parts.note: the answer is the chemical prefix that opens the name of a powerful liquid explosive used in dynamite

explanation.walkthrough: The 'preface' is a prefix: the first part of nitroglycerine, a powerful explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro is the shortened name for nitroglycerine and also the chemical prefix that introduces such compound names.

clue.text: Leave a lasting mark on Ed, and be a bit frightened because of it.

parts.note: to scar is to leave a lasting mark
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone left with a lasting mark from a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared is the everyday word for afraid, so a bit frightened fits it closely.

clue.text: Give a shout to Pierre, before Tim is confused about the start of Collected Reviews and Analysis.

indicators.note: the French shout comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: cri is French for a shout, as a Frenchman like Pierre would say

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter
confused means the letters of Tim and is are jumbled together

parts.note: the name taken as written
taken as written as part of the jumble

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its first letter, C

explanation.surface: Shouting to a Frenchman before a muddled Tim tackles a collection of reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for France, so the shout is French and comes 'before'. 'Confused' jumbles Tim and is (TIISM), and 'about' wraps them round 'the start of Collected' to make TICISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Criticism is the critical evaluation of works, which consists of reviews and analysis.

clue.text: Look, I'm a genius! Get the picture?

indicators.note: look tells the solver to inspect the words that follow for a word sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run through these words

explanation.surface: A boast of brilliance, then asking whether the listener understands.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: A final letter? Bear with it, possibly–it might be crossing in London.

definitions.text: it might be crossing in London

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: possibly means the word's letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: the word taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A last letter to sign off with, and a bear in tow, near a London road crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the bear into EBRA. A zebra crossing is the British name for a pedestrian crossing painted with black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white striped pedestrian crossing in British streets is named after the striped animal.

clue.text: One might find it overhead in place of 20.

definitions.text: One might find it overhead in place of 20.

parts.words: One might find it overhead in place of 20
parts.note: 20 is the French-built entry, so its place is France, where this headwear is worn on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 20 is built from French words, so 'place of 20' is France, home of the classic beret.
explanation.definitionFit: The beret is the soft round flat cap traditionally associated with France.

clue.text: Listens again to almost all of the rehearsal?

indicators.note: almost all means the end is clipped off the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hearing most of a rehearsal for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost all of' removes both final letters, not just one: REHEARSAL loses AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear something again is to listen to it a second time, giving a verb that takes an object like 'to'.

clue.text: Neither sharp nor flat, being the usual thing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in music, a note that is neither raised nor lowered
second meaning: what is normal or to be expected

explanation.walkthrough: Musical notation supplies the first sense; everyday speech the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a note with no accidental is called by this word, and in ordinary use it means normal or expected.

clue.text: The old writer offers a safe home to such as Teddy…

parts.note: safe here means sheltered from the wet, kept free of damp
a den is a bear's home, and a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A long-dead author giving shelter to a teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teddy' looks like a person, but it is the toy bear, whose wild cousins live in dens. 'Offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet and dramatist, an author of long ago.

clue.text: …and helped him out.

parts.note: continuing the previous clue, this is a plain description of having given someone a hand

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the clue before, but this half reads as a straightforward definition with no separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to give them help or support, which is what helping someone out means.
